findings.finding: Use f(S)=min LCM(a,b,c)=S−(k+1) with a=1,b=k|S−1. Smallest odd p|S−1 gives f(S)=(S−1)(p−1)/p. For odd S, p=smallest odd divisor of S−1 (≠(S−1)/2). Compute p for each S=M+c. g(c)=⌊N·f(S)/M⌋/N=⌊N(p−1)/p⌋/N. If p|N (p≤2025) →g=1−1/p; else g=1−(⌊N/p⌋+1)/N. N=2025!. p’s: c=0→5, 4M→11549, 1848374→11, 10162574→5081287, 265710644→29, 44636594→17. Sum fractions, reduce, compute (p+q) mod 99991 = 1554. Pitfalls: ensure p≠(S−1)/2, handle p>2025 case, ignore negligible ε.

We need f(n)=min lcm(a,b) with a+b=n‑1. Smallest divisor t>2 of S=n‑1 gives f=S·(t‑1)/t (t=4 if S≡0 mod4 else smallest odd divisor). For M=3^{2025!}, S_i=M+c‑1. Since 3^k≡1 (mod p) for any p≤2026, S_i≡c (mod p). Thus t_i = smallest divisor>2 of c (or 4 if c≡0 mod4). For c=0,4M: t=4. For c=1848374: t=11. For c=10162574: t=5081287 (prime, >2025). For c=265710644: t=4. For c=44636594: t=17. Compute K=2025!. For t≤2025, N_i=K−K/t. For t=5081287, N_i=K−⌊K/t⌋−1 (tiny ε from (c‑1)/M gives no carry). For c=4M, N=15K/4−1. Sum N_i, reduce by g=gcd(sum,K). p+q≡(sum/g)+(K/g) mod 99991. Result 89097. Pitfalls: ensure t=4 not 2; handle large t not dividing K; account for extra “‑1” in c=4M and large‑t case.

Reduced f(n) to min N with N|a,b (distinct) and a+b=n−N. Lower bound N≥6n/11 (using N/2,N/3). For n=M (3^{2025!}), M≡1 mod11 ⇒ N₀=6(M+10)/11 (multiple of6). Need a,b with sum=5N/6−δ (δ=10+11k). Show N₀ fails (δ=10 too small to adjust via divisors). Increase N by 6k until divisors allow sum reduction. Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·N/M⌋/2025! for each c, sum → p/q, find (p+q) mod 99991. (Key: f(n)=min N≥ceil(6n/11) multiple of6; adjust by k to satisfy divisor sum.)

f(n)=min lcm(a,b) with a+b=n‑1 ⇒ smallest divisor t>2 of S=n‑1 gives f=S·(t‑1)/t.  
M=3^K, K=2025!. For S=M+c‑1, t is the smallest divisor>2 of S.  
t’s: c=0→4; 4M→4; 1848374→11; 10162574→5081287; 265710644→4; 44636594→17.  
g(c)=⌊K·f/M⌋/K. For c>0 small, ⌊K·f/M⌋=K·(t‑1)/t; for c=0 subtract 1; for c=4M: ⌊…⌋=5·K·3/4‑1.  
Sum_N=Σ⌊K·f/M⌋= (3K/4‑1)+(15K/4‑1)+(10K/11)+(K‑K/5081287‑1)+(3K/4)+(16K/17).  
Reduce fraction ΣN/K → p/q; compute (p+q) mod 99991 = 6825.  
Pitfalls: c=0 gives negative ε → subtract 1; ensure t divides K for integer A; handle large t (5081287) via floor(K·(t‑1)/t).

We need f(S)=S−max{s=S mod l | s is sum of two distinct proper divisors of l}. For S=M+c (M=3^{2025!}) and any small c, max s≤~few 10³, while c≥0. Hence g(c)=⌊2025!·f(S)/M⌋/2025! =1 if s≤c, else (N−1)/N. Only c=0 gives s>0 ⇒g(0)=(N−1)/N. All other g=1. Sum=5+ (N−1)/N = (6N−1)/N ⇒p+q=7N−1. Compute (7·2025!−1) mod 99991 = 708.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b) with a+b=n‑1 ⇒ smallest divisor t>2 of S=n‑1 gives f=S·(t‑1)/t.  
M=3^k, k=2025!. For S=M+c‑1, t is smallest divisor>2 of S.  
t’s: c=0→4; 4M→4; 1848374→11; 10162574→5081287; 265710644→4; 44636594→17.  
g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025!. For t|K (K=2025!) ⇒ N=K·(t‑1)/t; adjust: c=0,4M,10162574 give –1 each; 4M adds extra 4·A.  
Sum N=ΣK·(t‑1)/t+4·(3K/4)−3. Reduce fraction N/K → p/q.  
p+q mod 99991 = 6825.   (Pitfall: c=0 gives –1; t may not divide K.)
